findings.title: Passing JS arrays into Prisma.sql with = ANY(...) produces invalid SQL
findings.body: In buildOrgAuthorizationCondition (line 164, `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))`) and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition (line 201, `("userId" = ANY(${userIdsFromTeam}))`), a plain JavaScript array is interpolated directly into a Prisma.sql template. Prisma's sql tag does NOT bind a JS array as a single Postgres array parameter — it expands array elements into separate positional placeholders (which is why Prisma.join exists for IN lists). So `ANY(${[1,2,3]})` becomes `ANY($1, $2, $3)`, which is a Postgres syntax/runtime error, or worse, `ANY($1)` with a scalar when the array has one element, silently matching nothing. The correct construction is `ANY(${Prisma.sql`ARRAY[${Prisma.join(teamIds)}]::int[]`})` or equivalent. The tests at lines 296 and 333 of the integration test compare against Prisma.sql templates built the same wrong way, so a deep-equal structural comparison can pass even though the generated query is broken when actually executed — and the PR description explicitly states the tests were never run.

findings.title: findMany() removed, breaking existing callers of the service
findings.body: The diff deletes the public `findMany(findManyArgs)` method, which accepted Prisma BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs and returned typed rows. It is replaced only by `getBaseConditions(): Promise<Prisma.Sql>`, which returns a raw SQL fragment that callers must embed into a hand-written raw query themselves. Any existing caller (e.g. insights repositories/routes that did `service.findMany({ select, orderBy, where })`) will fail to compile or, if untyped, fail at runtime. There is no deprecation shim or migration in this PR; the maintainer must verify every call site has been converted to $queryRaw with correct table names, select lists, and ordering before merging.

findings.title: Final test queries BookingTimeStatusDenormalized but only inserts into Booking
findings.body: The getBaseConditions test creates rows via `prisma.booking.create` and `prisma.eventType.create`, then runs `SELECT id FROM "BookingTimeStatusDenormalized" WHERE ...` expecting the user booking's id to be returned. Unless BookingTimeStatusDenormalized is a live view or is populated by a trigger/denormalization job that runs synchronously on booking insert, the table will not contain the new row and the assertion will fail (or pass vacuously if rows are absent). The PR author notes the tests were never executed due to runner configuration issues, so this is unverified.

findings.title: Caching tests deleted while caching behavior still exists in the service
findings.body: The previous test file contained a "Caching" describe block verifying that getAuthorizationConditions and getFilterConditions return cached results on repeated calls. The service still implements this caching (cachedAuthConditions / cachedFilterConditions in insightsBooking.ts lines 84-95), but all coverage for it was removed rather than updated to the Prisma.Sql format. This is a regression in test coverage for behavior that remains in production code, including the subtle case where a cached `null` filter condition must not trigger a rebuild.

findings.title: toEqual on Prisma.Sql objects may not validate actual SQL correctness
findings.body: All condition tests compare results with `expect(conditions).toEqual(Prisma.sql\`...\`)`. Prisma.Sql equality via vitest's deep equality only compares the internal strings/values structure; it does not verify the fragment is executable SQL. Combined with the fact that the author states the tests were never run, the expectations could match structurally while the produced SQL is invalid when executed (see the ANY(array) finding). At least one test per code path should execute the condition against the database via $queryRaw, as only the final test attempts to do.
